rulings.restated: Choose — [helper "Step 5, question 2: self-employed (Worksheet B)" = false → column (Step 5, 5)] [helper "Step 5, question 2: self-employed (Worksheet B)" = true → line 6 (eic.wsb_6)]
rulings.model: IRS Worksheet A says "Use this worksheet only if you answered “No” to Step 5, question 2. Otherwise, use Worksheet B." and its line 1 says "Enter your earned income from Step 5"; the restatement instead uses Worksheet B line 6 when the self-employed helper is true.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: representation; project retained. i1040gi p. 46, Worksheet A: "Use this worksheet only if you answered “No” to Step 5, question 2. Otherwise, use Worksheet B." and line 1: "Enter your earned income from Step 5."; p. 48, Worksheet B, line 6: "Enter your total earned income from Part 4, line 4b.", and lines 7 to 11 repeat Worksheet A lines 2 to 6 ("Look up the amount on line 6 above in the EIC Table", "Enter the amount from Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 11b", "Are the amounts on lines 8 and 6 the same?"). The project carries both worksheets on one set of printed lines and its English says so: "Enter your earned income from Step 5 (Worksheet A, line 1), or Worksheet B, line 6", taking the Step 5 amount when Step 5, question 2 is No and Worksheet B line 6 when it is Yes, with the citation "Worksheet A lines 2 to 6 are Worksheet B lines 7 to 11". For a Worksheet A filer the line is the source's line 1; for a Worksheet B filer it is the source's Worksheet B line 6, labelled as such. The model read the merged label as a misstatement of Worksheet A alone. No change.
